name: css_anim_perf_zombie
description: A SLIDING ZOMBIE NEVER FORCES A FULL FRAME. While an exit is on screen the renderer used to disable BOTH the skip and the incremental path - every zombie frame was a full composite. The per-frame truth is the union of the zombie's previous and current painted rects (restore the live frame where it was, paint it where it is). The fixture pins exactly that: the sidebar is an ABSOLUTE overlay, so unmounting it moves nothing else (no reconciliation move, no spring) - the only animation on screen is the exit, and every frame of it must report RECTS damage, never full. (A moved reference frame is also rect-damage now: its content bbox at the old and new matrix, about the frame origin - the previous blanket needs_full made every spring tick a full repaint.)

css: html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
#sidebar { position: absolute; left: 0px; top: 0px; width: 200px; height: 100%; background: #2255aa; -azul-animation-out: flyOutLeft 1s; }
html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
